# Provenance — threshold smoke-test fixtures

SCOPE: this record covers ONLY the four files named below. Other fixtures in this
directory (agent-overrides/, evidence-verify/) predate it and carry no provenance
record; that gap is pre-existing and is not claimed to be covered here.

## threshold-smoke-amendments.json
## threshold-smoke-expired-amendment.json
## threshold-smoke-risk-adjustment.json
## threshold-smoke-operational-requirement.json

AUTHORED test data, schema-confirmed. NOT real tool output, and this record says
so plainly rather than implying otherwise.

What is real and what is not:

  REAL      In the original three files, each requirementId was derived by running
            the repo's own command against the real Grype fixture rather than hand-typed:
              hdf amend draft --from hdf-fixtures/results/merge-grype.json \
                --type <type> --select <CVE> --expires 2099-12-31
            so an id that does not exist in that document cannot appear here.
            Source document: hdf-fixtures/results/merge-grype.json
            sha256 of that source as used: 3ea27a2d10c6718db07f2819740239d60dc5791e5186f4dd40a1dc15a9253004
            Captured: 2026-09-30

  AUTHORED  The substantive fields the draft leaves blank for a human —
            reason, appliedBy, status, impact, and the milestones. These are
            plausible governance text written for this test. No claim is made
            that any real assessor wrote them.

  CONFIRMED Both documents validate as hdf-amendments, and the applied set
            verifies clean and applies through the repo's own commands:
              hdf amend verify  -> Total 7, Valid 7, Expired 0, Invalid 0
              hdf amend apply   -> Applied 7 of 7 override(s)

Amendment types covered, and the remaining coverage limit:

  waiver              in force; moves its requirement to passed
  attestation         in force; manually verified as not reachable
  falsePositive       in force; resolves to notApplicable
  inherited           in force; adjudicated by a platform boundary
  poam                in force, with a pending milestone
  riskAdjustment      in force in its own file; expired in the second file

  operationalRequirement  in force in its own file; records the deviation without
                      changing status or impact, so the finding remains failed

  POA&M KIND          (remediation / mitigation / riskAcceptance /
                      vendorDependency) is NOT covered at this layer, and cannot
                      be: the kind lives on requirements[].poams[], and nothing
                      in the toolchain writes that array. Tracked as
                      hdf-libs-s4rmq.

A CONTESTED requirement is included deliberately: Grype/CVE-2020-13844 carries a
waiver applied 2024-06-01 and a POA&M applied 2025-01-01, so the newer entry must
govern its disposition. That is the resolution hdf-libs-wft3f.14 settled, and it
had no CLI-level coverage before this.

The expired fixture is separate because 'hdf amend apply' refuses a document
carrying ANY expired override, so deliberately-lapsed amendments cannot ride along with the
ones meant to be applied. threshold-smoke-expired-amendment.json carries two
kinds (riskAdjustment and waiver) so "lapsed" is not a single-type accident, and
exists to assert that refusal — the CLI-level half of "a lapsed amendment no
longer governs". The engine-level half is pinned by hdf-engine/testdata/
amendment-filter-cases.json and is not duplicated here.

Per hdf-libs policy these are FIXTURES, not amendments adjudicating any real
finding about this repository, so they carry no maintainer sign-off and must not
be read as a risk decision by anyone.

Dates: every in-force amendment uses the far-future constant 2099-12-31 so the
wall clock can never turn a passing test red; the expired ones use 2020-01-01 and
2020-06-30 because they assert expired behaviour.

## threshold-smoke-risk-adjustment.json — why a third file

An in-force riskAdjustment could not join the main corpus. merge-grype has ten
failing requirements; six are amended there, and the remainder has to stay
unadjudicated so the composite policy's rule has something to fire on. Adding a
seventh override consumed the last one and turned
TestSmoke_CompositePolicyGridAndRuleTogether red — measured, not assumed.

It carries one override against Grype/CVE-2022-42919, the only failing
requirement the main corpus leaves alone, re-scoring impact 0.7 -> 0.3 with an
expiry of 2099-12-31. Confirmed with `hdf amend verify`: All amendments are valid.

The requirement id appears twice in merge-grype (one CVE, two packages), so the
override governs both entries. That is the intended behaviour and the test
asserts against it rather than around it.

## threshold-smoke-operational-requirement.json — origin and validation

AUTHORED, schema-confirmed test data. It uses the same Grype/CVE-2022-42919 id
as the risk-adjustment fixture. The name, reason, appliedBy and dates are test
values, not an assessor's decision or real tool output. On 2026-11-03, the id
was independently confirmed against the source and sha256 recorded above with:
  hdf amend draft --from hdf-fixtures/results/merge-grype.json \
    --type operationalRequirement --select CVE-2022-42919 --expires 2099-12-31
The draft returned two entries with that id; the single override governs both.

Validated on 2026-11-03 with a freshly built CLI and its embedded schemas:
  hdf validate hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/testdata/threshold-smoke-operational-requirement.json --type amendments
    -> valid HDF amendments file
  hdf amend verify hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/testdata/threshold-smoke-operational-requirement.json
    -> Total 1, Valid 1, Expired 0, Invalid 0; chain not established
  hdf amend apply --results hdf-fixtures/results/merge-grype.json \
    --amendments hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/testdata/threshold-smoke-operational-requirement.json -o <output>
    -> Applied 1 of 1 override(s); merged output passes schema validation
  hdf query <output> --id Grype/CVE-2022-42919 --status failed --disposition operationalRequirement
    -> 2 matching requirements, both failed

TestSmoke_OperationalRequirementRecordsWithoutAdjudicating exercises this same
verify/apply/query flow. It checks that the deviation governs disposition while
the finding stays failed.
